interest: This document illustrates the U.S. State Department's tracking of Japanese naval infrastructure and maritime governance in the Kwantung Leased Territory during the early Manchukuo era. It highlights the reporting activities of diplomat John Carter Vincent at Dairen, monitoring Japanese regulatory changes and mapping for the Port Arthur naval station following the Manchurian Crisis. In addition, the cross-reference notation to 894c.156 provides historians with an essential archival index trail to locate the substantive translated regulations and accompanying map.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State List of Papers docket sheet for decimal file 894.34594C, which relates to naval and coaling stations, equipment, and vessel regulations in the Japanese-administered Kwantung Leased Territory. The sheet catalogues two communications sent in May 1933 by American consular officer John Carter Vincent in Dairen to the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo. These dispatches transmitted translations from the Kwantung Government Official Gazette of revised port regulations for the Port Arthur naval station, accompanied by a map and subsequent official textual corrections, with notations indicating cross-referencing to decimal file 894c.156.

subfiles.about: A Department of State List of Papers indexing two May 1933 consular dispatches from Dairen concerning revised port regulations for the Port Arthur naval station.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet lists two dispatches prepared in May 1933 by U.S. Consul John Carter Vincent in Dairen for the American Embassy in Tokyo. The first entry, dated May 13, 1933, records a translation from the Kwantung Government Official Gazette No. 890 containing revised port regulations for the Port Arthur naval station along with an attached map, noted as transferred to file 894c.156. The second entry, dated May 24, 1933, documents subsequent corrections issued by the Kwantung Government to the original published text of the regulations.
